customer.definition: The account record. Orders and Cases say customer too but carry only the customerId; nothing about a person lives outside Identity

relationships.description: Offers keep their own SKU list translated from catalogue events
The buy box price is indexed as published
Checkout is the offer API's main customer and gets a say in its contract
Order lines carry the offer id they were bought from; Orders never reads Offers back, so the coupling is identity only and neither side plays a role in an exchange that does not happen
Refunds are requested through the payments API
The order id is attached to the payment on OrderPlaced so captures at dispatch can find it
Ad groups advertise catalogue products by id
The warehouse turns orders into its own fulfilment orders
Dispatches and returns flow back onto the order
Verdicts come back as events; orders never call fraud synchronously
Roles on the consumption were never agreed; see the role-coherence warning
Agents need order reads and returns; Orders commits to that contract
The nightly export is translated; nobody touches the legacy tables directly
TrackingLabel format and scan events are one shared library

comments.text: TrackingLabel and the scan event codes live in @rivermart/tracking, imported by both.
The label format is a carrier standard, so neither side can own it; the kernel is the cheapest place to keep it in step.

relationships.description: The results page is one product owned by two teams

comments.text: Organic ranking and sponsored slots are blended in one service; neither team deploys the results page alone.

relationships.description: Vendors and sellers are kept apart by policy; no shared identity, no shared data
